claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. His name is Alex and he's 7 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Now I have a few more questions to assess your eligibility.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Are you responsible for Alex? This usually means either:
- You live with him, or
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him, for example on food, clothes or pocket money

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute money towards his upkeep - I help with things like clothes and other expenses for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. Since Alex lives with someone else, I have a couple of follow-up questions.

How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions? 

For context, to remain eligible for Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else, you generally need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you, that's helpful. Your contribution of £50 per week is above the Child Benefit payment threshold, which is good.

Just a couple more questions:

1. Is there anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
2. Is Alex in any form of local council care, or is the local council paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. 

However, Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex being in local authority care. This is important information.

Could you tell me:

1. How long exactly has Alex been in care? (specifically, has it been more or less than 8 weeks?)
2. Does Alex spend any time at home with you - for example, does he spend at least 24 hours a week at home, or 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 or more days in a row at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in care for about 12 weeks now. He doesn't come home to stay with me - he's there full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail for your eligibility.

When a child has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you would usually no longer be entitled to Child Benefit. However, there is an exception: you may still be able to receive Child Benefit if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home.

Since Alex has been in care for 12 weeks (which is more than 8 weeks) and he doesn't spend any time at home with you, unfortunately this means you would not currently be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex under the standard rules.

However, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again in the future if circumstances change - for example, if Alex starts spending 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row at home with you.

Let me provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of my findings:

**For Alex (age 7):** ❌ Not Eligible

**Reason:** While you meet several eligibility criteria:
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex is under 16
- ✅ You contribute £50 per week towards his upkeep (above the Child Benefit threshold)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

The issue is that Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks, which exceeds the 8-week threshold. After 8 weeks in care, you're usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit unless the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home. Since Alex is in care full-time and doesn't spend any time at home with you, this exception doesn't apply.

**Looking ahead:** If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he starts spending 2 nights in a row each week or 7 or more consecutive days at home with you - you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. I would recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly if his situation changes.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?
